record.paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: Does the directed s-t connectivity problem admit a simple, direct proof that it belongs to catalytic logspace CL?

evidence.quote: Problem 3. Give a simple, direct proof of STConn ∈ CL.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. The class L of logspace decidable languages consists of those decided by a deterministic Turing machine using O(log n) work-tape cells on inputs of length n. The class CL of catalytic logspace languages is defined as follows: a Turing machine has, in addition to its standard read-only input tape and O(log n)-bit read/write work tape, an auxiliary "catalytic" tape of length 2^{O(log n)} = poly(n) which is initialized with an arbitrary string w. The machine may read and write freely on the catalytic tape during its computation, but is required to restore the catalytic tape to its original content w by the end of the computation, regardless of w. A language L is in CL if there is such a machine that decides L correctly on every input for every initial catalytic content w.

The directed s-t connectivity problem, STConn, takes as input a directed graph G = (V, E) together with two designated vertices s, t ∈ V, and asks whether there is a directed path from s to t in G. It is known that STConn ∈ CL (this follows from the inclusion of nondeterministic logspace in CL via known techniques). However, the established proofs of STConn ∈ CL proceed indirectly through general simulation theorems.

Problem. Exhibit a simple, direct catalytic-logspace algorithm that decides STConn. More precisely, describe an explicit Turing machine with an O(log n) work tape and a poly(n)-length catalytic tape, together with a self-contained proof that for every initial catalytic content w, the machine correctly decides whether t is reachable from s in the input directed graph, and leaves the catalytic tape equal to w upon halting.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work by Cook and Pyne ("Efficient Catalytic Graph Algorithms", arXiv:2509.06209, 2025) presents direct catalytic-logspace algorithms for directed s-t connectivity, including a deterministic catalytic algorithm running in Õ(n^3 m) time using O(log n) workspace and Õ(n^2) catalytic space. This is widely described as giving the simplest known direct proof that STConn ∈ CL, though whether it fully satisfies the informal "simple, direct" criterion is a matter of interpretation.

status_evidence.title: Efficient Catalytic Graph Algorithms
status_evidence.snippet: A randomized catalytic algorithm for s→t connectivity running in Õ(nm) time, and a deterministic catalytic algorithm running in Õ(n^3 m) time.
status_evidence.claim: Provides direct catalytic logspace algorithms for directed s-t connectivity.

status_evidence.title: Tree-eval, catalytic computation, simulating time with square-root space
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion describes a direct catalytic algorithm for directed reachability based on maintaining shifted path-count registers and reversing them to restore the catalytic tape.
status_evidence.claim: A simple direct proof idea for STConn ∈ CL is described in expository discussion.
